In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; MountRules.ControlledTurn answered the turn instead of declining for what an action does (`if (false && askingWhatAnActionDoes is { } asked)`); this test went red and no other did.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; MountRules.Control declined only a stated lack of training (`if (creature.Training == MountTraining.NotTrained)`), so a mount whose training nothing states was controlled; this test went red, and so did mount-control-requires-training's own tests.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; MountRules.ControlledTurn dropped the rulings its input relied on (`OwnerRulings.None` in place of `OwnerRulings.InOrder(control.Rulings)`), so a turn resting on Brandon's ruling named none; this test went red and no other did.
